tools.name: check_tls
tools.description: Scan a public host's TLS from the internet: certificate validity, chain completeness, expiry date, hostname match, enabled protocols (TLS 1.0–1.3), cipher suites, HSTS. Use when browsers show certificate errors, before/after renewing or rotating a certificate, or to confirm old TLS versions are disa

tools.name: check_http
tools.description: Request a public URL from outside your network and inspect the HTTP layer: status code, full redirect chain, security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy…), caching and compression headers. Use to debug redirect loops, unexpected status codes or missing heade

tools.name: check_email_domain
tools.description: Audit a mail domain as other mail servers see it: MX, SPF (including the 10-DNS-lookup limit), DKIM, DMARC policy, PTR / forward-confirmed reverse DNS, SMTP STARTTLS on the MX hosts, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, BIMI. Use when mail lands in spam or bounces, after changing mail provider or DNS, or before tighte

tools.name: check_dns
tools.description: Resolve a name at several public resolvers (Google, Cloudflare, Quad9, …) and compare their answers. Use after changing DNS records to check propagation, or when some users reach a different IP or get NXDOMAIN. Use check_email_domain instead for SPF/DKIM/DMARC analysis. Returns per-resolver answers,

tools.name: check_port
tools.description: Check from the internet whether TCP ports of a public host are open, closed or filtered. Use to verify firewall / security group rules, or to find out why a service works locally but is unreachable from outside. Only public addresses are accepted; this does not test the application behind the port (

tools.name: check_ip
tools.description: Look up an IP address or ASN: owner organization, announced prefix, PTR (reverse DNS), RPKI validity and geolocation. Use to identify who is behind an address seen in logs or headers, or to check PTR / RPKI for a mail or BGP issue. Does not test reachability (use check_port).

tools.name: check_dnsbl
tools.description: Check whether an IP address or a domain is on email blocklists (DNSBL/RBL): Spamhaus ZEN and DBL, SpamCop, Barracuda, UCEPROTECT, Mailspike, SURBL, URIBL and others. For a domain, its own name is checked on domain lists and its A/AAAA addresses on IP lists. Use when mail bounces with 'listed'/'block

tools.name: check_domain_expiry
tools.description: Look up a domain's registration in the registry (RDAP, or WHOIS for .ru/.su/.рф): expiry date and days left, registrar, creation date, EPP status codes (clientHold, redemptionPeriod, transfer locks…) with explanations, nameservers and DNSSEC. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_http, check_email_domain, check_ip, check_dnsbl · Private data: check_dns, check_domain_expiry · Public sink: check_http, check_email_domain, check_dnsbl.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_http, check_email_domain, check_ip, check_dnsbl · Private data: check_dns, check_domain_expiry · Public sink: check_http, check_email_domain, check_dnsbl

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
